newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in heavy turnover.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in heavy turnover.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Monday amid heavy trading by institutional investors, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.14 pct to 102.57
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 101.59.
Volume was a high 170 million shekels.

"Bond prices are continuing to rise broadly and the market is showing strength," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities. "The main reason for the rise is that mutual and provident funds have increased their activity in the market."
"The rise in bond prices is not logical at all. The budget deficit is rising and tax revenues are expected to decline. In the end the government will be forced to issue more bonds," Scharia added.
Preliminary figures released by the Treasury on Sunday showed that the budget deficit rose in January to 1.3 billion shekels, which was bigger than projections.

"The sharp rise of the stock market had no impact on bonds, which continued to rise sharply. Inflation-linked bonds were today's main gainers with yields falling to only 4.1-4.2 percent," said Miri Dagan at Clal Insurance.

"The market is not very attractive and the activity of the institutional investors is forcing yields downward. I believe that this trend will continue with yields on long CPI-linked bonds falling to 4 percent," Scharia added.
Dagan said unlinked bonds also rose because some investors believe that over the long run interest rates would continue to decline.

Traders said dollar-linked bonds rose after the shekel fell to a new all time-low against the dollar. On Monday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3210 shekels against 3.3140 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
